preconditions.expression: all(c in '0123456789-' for c in stdin)
preconditions.description: The input string consists only of digits and hyphens.
The length of the input string is between 1 and 100,000 characters.

postconditions.expression: stdout == apocalypse_date and apocalypse_date is not None
postconditions.description: The output is the unique date in 'dd-mm-yyyy' format that appears strictly more times than any other valid date in the input string.

postconditions.expression: apocalypse_date is not None and is_valid_date(apocalypse_date)
postconditions.description: The output date is valid: year in [2013, 2015], month in [1, 12], and day valid for the month (non-leap years).

postconditions.expression: count > max(count_other for date_other, count_other in date_counts.items() if date_other != apocalypse_date)
postconditions.description: The output date's occurrence count is strictly greater than any other valid date's count in the input.

invariants.expression: is_valid_date(date) == (2013 <= int(date[6:10]) <= 2015 and 1 <= int(date[3:5]) <= 12 and 1 <= int(date[0:2]) <= 31 and is_day_valid(int(date[0:2]), int(date[3:5])))
invariants.description: A date is valid if its year is between 2013 and 2015, month is between 1 and 12, and day is valid for the month (non-leap years).
A day is valid for a month if it does not exceed the number of days in that month (non-leap years).
